clue.text: Junior sports team member lapping graduate, a blue

indicators.note: lapping means wrapping round, so the first piece encloses the second

parts.note: a colt is a young player in a junior side
Bachelor of Arts, the standard graduate abbreviation

explanation.surface: A youth-team player runs a lap ahead of a university graduate, perhaps an Oxbridge sporting Blue.
explanation.walkthrough: A colt is a young player in a junior side. 'A blue' looks like a sports honour, which fits the surface, but it is a shade of colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Cobalt is a deep, intense shade of blue pigment, named after the metal used to make it.

clue.text: I'm so embarrassed wearing new lace undergarment

indicators.note: to be wearing something is to have it round you, so one group of letters sits inside another
someone embarrassed is flustered and thrown into disorder, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

indicators.note: new means made over, so these four letters are put in a fresh order

parts.note: the letters taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone blushes at being seen in brand-new lace underwear.
explanation.walkthrough: There are two separate anagrams here, each with its own signal, and the first result then sits inside the second.
explanation.definitionFit: A camisole is a light sleeveless bodice worn under clothing, so it is a kind of undergarment.

clue.text: Sash and girl's handkerchief

parts.note: a sash is a band of cloth
a girl's name; the 's just joins it on

explanation.surface: A girl's outfit includes a sash and a matching handkerchief.
explanation.definitionFit: A bandanna is a large coloured handkerchief, often worn knotted round the head or neck.

clue.text: Feudal lord, say, in tale

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other, here a short abbreviation sitting within a word

parts.note: a tale can mean a falsehood
'say' means for example, abbreviated e.g.

explanation.surface: A feudal lord appears, for instance, in some old story.
explanation.definitionFit: In the feudal system a liege was the superior lord to whom vassals owed allegiance and service.

clue.text: Options involving cold sweets

indicators.note: something involving another thing takes it in, so a letter goes inside the word

parts.note: options are choices
C for cold, as on a tap

explanation.surface: A menu of chilled desserts offers several options.
explanation.walkthrough: A choc ice is a British bar of ice cream coated in chocolate, so 'sweets' here is used in the dessert sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Choc ices are chocolate-coated ice cream bars, desserts that count as sweets in the British pudding sense.

clue.text: One clinging on to attacker in confusion?

parts.note: one who clings or hugs
a street robber who attacks

explanation.surface: A victim clings desperately to a robber amid chaos.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful split of the hyphenated word into two people.
explanation.definitionFit: Hugger-mugger is an old adverb and adjective meaning in disorder or muddle, as well as in secret.

clue.text: Cleaner, by a stop, caught bus

parts.note: a char, or charwoman, is a cleaner
taken as written
to stop is to ban
c is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A cleaner, standing by a stop, catches the bus.
explanation.walkthrough: A char is an old British word for a cleaning woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A charabanc was an early open motor coach used for outings, so a kind of bus.

clue.text: Pop briefly coming round in hospital

indicators.note: coming round something means arriving to surround it, so the shortened word encloses the other
briefly means cut short, so the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a pop is a short sharp sound, a click

indicators.note: round here turns the small word that follows it about, so it reads backwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Dad pays a short visit to someone recovering in hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pop' tempts as father; it is a sound. 'Round' does double work, turning the little word about as the shortened sound goes round it.
explanation.definitionFit: A clinic is a medical establishment or hospital department where patients are treated.

clue.text: Nurse demanding cut is bandaged

indicators.note: a bandaged thing is wrapped round, so one piece sits inside the other
cut means trimmed, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: demanding means strict or stern
taken as written

explanation.surface: A strict nurse insists that the cut be dressed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut' looks like a wound in the surface; it is the signal to trim a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: In British hospitals a sister is a senior nurse in charge of a ward.

clue.text: Vexation shown by first of mares in trough

indicators.note: first of means only the opening letter of the next word is used

parts.note: the opening letter of mares
vexation is anger

explanation.surface: Horses show irritation when gathered at the feeding trough.
explanation.definitionFit: A manger is a long open box or trough from which horses and cattle eat.

clue.text: I fly with one American martyr

parts.note: taken as written
a gnat is a small fly
Roman numeral one
US is short for American, as in the United States

explanation.surface: Someone claims to be flying alongside a martyred American.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fly' looks like a verb but is the insect.
explanation.definitionFit: St Ignatius of Antioch was an early Christian bishop martyred in Rome, thrown to wild beasts.

clue.text: Plaintive cry on ship from most senior male director, perhaps

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the alarm shouted when someone falls into the sea
second meaning, read literally: a man placed over the rest of the board of directors

explanation.walkthrough: The second half is whimsical: a chairman is a man set over the board. 'Perhaps' signals that it is only one example.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is the standard shipboard alarm raised when a person has fallen into the water.

clue.text: Possible outcome of chess game in flat against pal

parts.note: flat, as of beer or bread, means stale
a mate is a pal

explanation.surface: Two friends play chess at home in their flat and it ends in a draw.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flat' looks like an apartment; it means past its best.
explanation.definitionFit: Stalemate is the drawn position in chess where the player to move has no legal move but is not in check.

clue.text: Assistant catching small stage whisper

indicators.note: catching means taking hold of, so one word encloses a single letter

parts.note: an aide is an assistant
S is the size abbreviation for small

explanation.surface: A theatre assistant overhears a quiet stage whisper.
explanation.definitionFit: An aside is a remark an actor makes to the audience, supposedly unheard by the other characters.

clue.text: Spam on chalet menu abroad

indicators.note: abroad suggests being scattered widely, so the letters are spread into a new order

parts.note: the twelve letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Tinned Spam turns up on the menu at a ski chalet overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spam' looks like junk email, but here it is the brand of tinned meat.
explanation.definitionFit: Spam is the best-known brand of tinned pork luncheon meat, so the brand stands for the product.

clue.text: Poser they solved at once

indicators.note: something solved has been worked out, so the letters are worked into their right arrangement

parts.note: the nine letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A puzzle that was cracked immediately.
explanation.definitionFit: Hey presto is a conjuror's exclamation for something appearing instantly, as if by magic.

clue.text: Longs to nurse poorly Greek hero

indicators.note: to nurse is to hold close, so one word is cradled inside another

parts.note: to long for is to ache for
poorly means unwell

explanation.surface: A wounded Greek hero yearns to tend the sick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poorly' is British everyday speech for unwell.
explanation.definitionFit: Achilles was the great Greek warrior of the Trojan War, hero of the Iliad.

clue.text: One supporting that lady during a depression

indicators.note: during means within the span of, so one word sits inside another

parts.note: a dent is a depression in a surface
her refers to a woman

explanation.surface: Someone stood by a woman through a bout of depression.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Depression' suggests low mood; it is a hollow.
explanation.definitionFit: An adherent is a follower or supporter of a cause, party or person.

clue.text: Drug I dig, scarcely worried

indicators.note: worried means agitated or shaken up, so the letters are disturbed into a new order

parts.note: the twelve letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A user admits to being barely bothered about drugs.
explanation.definitionFit: Lysergic acid is the compound from which the hallucinogen LSD (lysergic acid diethylamide) is made.

clue.text: Stop talking about large American at university

parts.note: c is short for circa, about
L is the size abbreviation for large
Am. is an abbreviation for American
in British usage one is up at university

explanation.surface: A big American student falls silent.
explanation.walkthrough: Being 'up' at university is British usage, from going up to Oxford or Cambridge.
explanation.definitionFit: To clam up is an idiom for refusing to speak, shutting tight like a clam's shell.

clue.text: A second omen for delegate

parts.note: taken as written
s is the abbreviation for second
an omen is a sign

explanation.surface: A second portent is taken as a sign for someone sent to represent others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Delegate' is the verb here, not the person.
explanation.definitionFit: To delegate a task is to allot or hand it to someone else, which is to assign it.

clue.text: No-hoper, not as far away after leader's gone

indicators.note: with the leader gone the word loses its first letter

parts.note: not as far away means nearer

explanation.surface: A no-hoper falls further behind once the front-runner is out of the race.
explanation.definitionFit: A loser is someone habitually unsuccessful, the sort with no hope of winning.

clue.text: Subsistence level reportedly raised before row

indicators.note: reportedly means as said by others, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: raised, as children or animals, means bred
a row is a line

explanation.surface: Reports that someone was brought up before a family quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' pulls towards an argument; it is a straight line.
explanation.definitionFit: The breadline is the poverty threshold, the barest minimum income needed to live.

clue.text: Amusing puppet round end of pier

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so the first word goes about a single letter

parts.note: a puppet is a kind of doll

indicators.note: end of means only the last letter of the next word is kept

parts.note: the final letter of pier

explanation.surface: A Punch and Judy show at the end of the pier is funny.
explanation.definitionFit: Droll means amusing in a dry, odd or whimsical way.

clue.text: Chief support provided by mother during visit

parts.note: ma is mother
during means in, as in 'in the night'
a visit is a stay

explanation.surface: Mum provides crucial support while staying over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'During' looks like an insertion signal; here it just supplies IN.
explanation.definitionFit: A mainstay is a chief support; literally the stay holding up a ship's mainmast.

clue.text: Miner's tailless dog

indicators.note: without its tail, the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a collier is a coal miner

explanation.surface: A coal miner owns a dog with no tail.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is': the miner, cut short, is the dog.
explanation.definitionFit: A collie is a breed of sheepdog originating in Scotland.

clue.text: Apple dessert, lacking in taste after roast

indicators.note: after says the first-named piece follows the second, so the clue's order is flipped in the answer

parts.note: to roast or pan is to criticise harshly
dowdy means dull and unfashionable

explanation.surface: A dessert served after the Sunday roast proves bland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Roast' suggests a meal; it means to slate a review.
explanation.definitionFit: Pandowdy is an American baked pudding of sliced apples under a crust.

clue.text: Secret press

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a cupboard, an old sense of press

explanation.walkthrough: 'Press' looks like journalism or a verb; it is an old word for a cupboard.
explanation.definitionFit: Closet works as an adjective meaning covert and as a noun for a cupboard or small storage room.
